parts.text: In this experiment you will investigate the refraction of light through a transparent block. Record all of your observations and answers on page 6 of your Answer Booklet. Carry out the following instructions referring to Fig. 4.1, Fig. 4.2 and Fig. 4.3. Fig. 4.1 Fig. 4.2 Fig. 4.3

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Draw a straight line approximately in the centre of the sheet of plain paper.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Stand the transparent block on the paper with one of its shortest sides over the line as shown in Figs 4.1 and 4.2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Look, with one eye closed, vertically down through the block. You will see the image within the block of the pencil line you have drawn on the paper.

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Place the optics pin horizontally with its point touching the transparent block approximately in the centre so that the pencil line and the pin appear to form one straight line. Move your eye slightly in a horizontal plane, as shown in Fig. 4.1. You will see that the image of the pencil line and the pin appear to separate.

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Continue to look vertically down through the block and slowly move the pin downwards until you find a position where the pin and the image of the pencil line do not separate when you move your eye.

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Without changing the position of the point of the pin that is touching the block, measure and record the vertical distance x between the paper and the pin.

sensible h value (typical block: 10 cm)

parts.text: (g) Measure and record the height h of the transparent block.

parts.text: (h) Calculate the refractive index n of the material of the block using the equation n = h ––––– h – x .

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Stand the transparent block on the paper with one of its longest sides over the line as shown in Fig. 4.3.

parts.label: k
parts.text: (k) Calculate the average value of the refractive index n .

parts.label: l
parts.text: (l) To obtain a reliable value for the vertical distance x between the paper and the pin it is important that the pin is horizontal. Explain briefly with the aid of a diagram how you checked that the pin was horizontal.
